packs.title: Coast & Coffee
packs.promise: Explore fishpond engineering, coastal parks, a working coffee farm and South Kona’s cultural landscape.

q.s: Make a coastline drawing from dry ground.
st: Use open county park ground in daylight. No beach purchase or water activity is required. Park only in marked public spaces.
Choose an open dry park position well behind the wave reach. Draw three broad bands: land, breaking water and the distant horizon. Use only shapes you actually see.
Add a small detail to each band. Circle the detail that best locates your drawing on this particular shore.

q.t: Seed to Cup in Four Scenes
q.s: Tell the coffee process as a four-panel story.
st: Regular guided tour is free, about 45–60 minutes. Arrive at 81-6581 Māmalahoa Highway by 08:45 for a planned 09:00 start; daily tour starts currently run 08:30–14:00, no reservation required. Allow 75 minutes for check-in, tour and notes.
Join the regular guided visit. Choose four stages the guide actually explains; use words or small drawings to show how the crop changes between them.
Finish with one question the visit answered. Sampling and buying coffee are optional; the process story is your proof.

q.s: Read the relationship between two protected spaces.
st: Use ordinary admitted park entry. Standard private-vehicle entry $20, motorcycle $15 or walk-in $10; qualifying passes and age eligibility apply. Cashless payment. Gates open 08:15–sunset; plan this visit before the afternoon trail.

Follow the signed self-guided visitor route. From permitted positions, note one feature associated with the Royal Grounds and one that helps define the puʻuhonua; use the park interpretation for their meaning.
Make a two-column note: what you saw and what you learned. Finish with one question you would like to ask a ranger.

packs.title: Village by the Bay
packs.promise: Explore a compact village through a banyan, a royal shoreline, stone landmarks and small acts of making.

q.s: Find five colors without taking anything home.
st: Use the established public beach approach near Kailua Pier and remain on open dry beach. No hotel service, rental or purchase is required.
Reach the public dry beach by its ordinary public approach. Choose five visible colors across sand, water, stone, plants or sky; describe them without collecting material.
Arrange the colors from nearest to furthest away and give your palette a short title based on what you observed.

q.t: An Object with a Royal Story
q.s: Let one museum object lead your visit.
st: Plan Wednesday–Saturday, 10:00–15:00; last entry 14:30, major holidays closed. Reserve a self-guided visit around 14:00 in advance; walk-ins depend on availability. Standard nonresident adult 18–64 $16; other rates apply. No parking at the palace.
On your admitted self-guided visit, select one displayed object with an available label. Record its name or type and two visible details without touching it.
Explain how the label changes your first impression. Use notes if photography is restricted; no particular room or object is promised.

q.t: A Park Between Street and Sea
q.s: Design a tiny gathering place on paper.
st: The county states the park remains open with restricted work areas. Check current barriers on arrival and use only open public ground; completion of all works is not assumed.
Use an open dry public area of the park, outside work fencing. Note one existing way the space connects street, people and sea.
On paper, design a gathering space using three elements you actually observed. Explain how your arrangement would keep the public route clear; do not move anything.
